items.question: I bought new shoes at the ___ .
explanations: 'Shoes shop' wrongly makes the first noun plural.
Correct! The first noun stays singular: 'shoe shop'.
'Shoe's shop' adds an unnecessary apostrophe.
'Shoes' shop' is also wrong.

items.question: There are three ___ on this street.
explanations: 'Bus's stops' adds an incorrect apostrophe.
'Buses stops' wrongly pluralises the first noun.
'Bus stop' is singular but 'three' needs a plural.
Correct! Only the last word takes the plural: 'bus stops'.

items.question: It's only a ___ walk from here.
explanations: 'Five minute's' adds an incorrect apostrophe.
'Five-minutes' wrongly keeps the plural.
Correct! A number + noun before a noun is singular: 'a five-minute walk'.
'Five minutes' is plural and has no hyphen.

items.question: Both my ___ came to the wedding.
explanations: Correct! The main noun 'mother' takes the plural: 'mothers-in-law'.
'Mother-in-laws' pluralises the wrong word.
'Mothers-in-laws' pluralises twice.
'Mother-in-law's' is a possessive.

items.question: Can you pass me a ___ ?
explanations: 'Coffee's cup' adds an incorrect apostrophe.
'Coffees cup' wrongly pluralises the first noun.
Correct! First noun singular: 'coffee cup'.
'Cup coffee' is the wrong order.

items.question: We stayed in a hotel with two ___ .
explanations: 'Swimming pool's' adds an incorrect apostrophe.
'Swim pools' is not the usual compound: we say 'swimming pool'.
'Swimming pool' is singular but 'two' needs a plural.
Correct! Only the last word is plural: 'swimming pools'.

items.question: She's a ___ girl.
explanations: 'Ten-years-old' wrongly keeps the plural.
Correct! Singular, hyphenated before the noun: 'a ten-year-old girl'.
'Ten year olds' is missing hyphens and is plural.
'Ten years old' is fine after 'is', but before a noun we say 'ten-year-old'.

items.question: Put your dirty clothes in the ___ .
explanations: Correct! Compound noun, first part singular: 'washing machine'.
'Wash machine' is not the usual compound: we say 'washing machine'.
'Washed machine' is wrong: the first part is the -ing form, 'washing'.
'Machine washing' is the wrong order.

items.question: Choose the correct version of: 'It's a three-days trip.'
explanations: 'Three days trip' keeps the plural and drops the hyphen.
Correct! Number + noun before a noun is singular: 'a three-day trip'.
'Three-day's' adds an incorrect apostrophe.
'Three-days trip' is incorrect.

items.question: In a compound noun, which part is normally made plural?
explanations: You don't pluralise both.
The first noun stays singular.
Correct! Only the final element takes the plural (bus stops).
Plurals do change the last word.
